**Nyingchi** ([Tibetan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tibetan_script "Tibetan script"): ཉིང་ཁྲི་གྲོང་ཁྱེར།, [Wylie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wylie_transliteration "Wylie transliteration"): nying khri grong khyer**Linzhi** ([Chinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simplified_Chinese_characters "Simplified Chinese characters"): ; [pinyin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pinyin "Pinyin"): _Línzhī_) or **Nyingtri** , is a [prefecture-level city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prefecture-level_city "Prefecture-level city") in the southeast of the [Tibet Autonomous Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tibet_Autonomous_Region "Tibet Autonomous Region") in [China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China "China"). The administrative seat of Nyingchi is [Bayi District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bayi_District "Bayi District").
Nyingchi is the location of [Buchu Monastery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buchu_Monastery "Buchu Monastery").
## History
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nyingchi&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]
The area around Nyingchi has been settled since Tibet's [prehistoric era](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prehistoric_era "Prehistoric era").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyingchi#cite_note-x246-2) Researchers discovered several human bones and burial groups from the [Neolithic Age](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neolithic "Neolithic") near the [Nyang River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyang_River "Nyang River") in the 1970s, suggesting that humans in Nyingchi were engaged in slash-and-burn agriculture and led a relatively sedentary lifestyle as early as 4,000-5,000 years ago.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyingchi#cite_note-k583-3) Unearthed artifacts, including net pendants and arrowheads, indicate that the inhabitants of this region, along the ancient Nyang River, [Yarlung Zangbo River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yarlung_Zangbo_River "Yarlung Zangbo River"), and ancient lakes, were involved in both cultivation and fishing activities along the riverbanks.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyingchi#cite_note-y709-4)
Initially, Nyingchi was under the dominion of the King of [Kongpo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kongpo "Kongpo"). In the [Sakyapa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sakyapa "Sakyapa") and [Phagmodrupa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phagmodrupa "Phagmodrupa") periods (13th-16th centuries), Nyingchi emerged as the dominion of the [Karma Kagyu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karma_Kagyu "Karma Kagyu") sect of [Tibetan Buddhism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tibetan_Buddhism "Tibetan Buddhism"). Subsequently, in the 17th century, the [Ganden Podrang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ganden_Podrang "Ganden Podrang") was instituted, leading to the partitioning of Nyingchi into the territories of three families including Ngapoi. Nyingchi was further subdivided into Zela (རྩེ་ལ་), Qomo (ཇོ་མོ་), Xoka (ཞོ་ཁ་), and Gyamda (རྒྱ་མདའ་) [dzongs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dzong "Dzong"). The [Bomê region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Powo "Kingdom of Powo") had long been governed by the local leader Kanam Depa and was in a condition of secession.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyingchi#cite_note-5)
In 1931, the Tibetan government annexed Bomê and partitioned it into two administrative divisions: Bodoi and [Bomê](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bom%C3%AA_County "Bomê County"), while the Mêdog area was reclassified as [Mêdog dzong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M%C3%AAdog_County "Mêdog County").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyingchi#cite_note-u076-6)
Tibet was annexed by China in May 1951. In January 1960, the Tagong Special Department was established, and in February 1960, it was restructured as the Nyingchi Prefecture, with the Special Department located in Nyingchi County.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyingchi#cite_note-f284-7) In March 2015, [State Council of China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_Council_of_China "State Council of China") sanctioned the dissolution of Nyingchi Prefecture and the creation of Nyingchi City at the prefecture level, as well as the dissolution of Nyingchi County and the establishment of [Bayi District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bayi_District "Bayi District").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyingchi#cite_note-d897-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyingchi#cite_note-s366-9)

### Tourism
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nyingchi&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Tourism")]
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2e/%E8%8D%89%E5%8E%9F%EF%BC%8C%E9%9B%AA%E5%B1%B1_-_panoramio.jpg/250px-%E8%8D%89%E5%8E%9F%EF%BC%8C%E9%9B%AA%E5%B1%B1_-_panoramio.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:%E8%8D%89%E5%8E%9F%EF%BC%8C%E9%9B%AA%E5%B1%B1_-_panoramio.jpg)Nyingchi mountains
The average elevation of Nyingchi is 3,040 meters (9,974 feet), which is the lowest compared with the other prefectures in Tibet. The relatively low elevation compared to other regions of the Tibetan plateau yields a lower risk of [altitude sickness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Altitude_sickness "Altitude sickness"). [Guangdong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangdong "Guangdong") province announced in 2012 that it plans to invest more than RMB 400 million (US$63 million) in Nyingchi's tourism industry. According to the plan, Guangdong will help build 22 "prosperous model villages" in Nyingchi in counties such as [Bomê](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bom%C3%AA_County "Bomê County") and [Zayü](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zay%C3%BC_County "Zayü County").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyingchi#cite_note-10)
Nyingchi Convention and Exhibition Center ([Chinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_language "Chinese language"): ; [Tibetan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tibetan_script "Tibetan script"): ལིན་ཀྲི་ཧྲུའེ་ལམ་ཞིབ་འཛིན་ཁང་[Chinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_language "Chinese language"): ), is a convention center in the city. The province of Guandong contributed funds to the building of the center.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyingchi#cite_note-Xizang2015-05-04-11) In 2018, the opening ceremony of the first Trans-Himalaya Extreme Cycling Race was held at the center's square.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyingchi#cite_note-Zhang2018-10-16-12) In 2023, young artists from [Zhuhai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhuhai "Zhuhai"), [Hong Kong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hong_Kong "Hong Kong") and [Macao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macao "Macao") went to Nyingchi for performances and exchanges.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyingchi#cite_note-Yuan2023-08-04-13)
## Transportation
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nyingchi&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Transportation")]
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/51/Nyingchi_airport_June_2019.jpg/250px-Nyingchi_airport_June_2019.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Nyingchi_airport_June_2019.jpg)[Nyingchi Mainling Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyingchi_Mainling_Airport "Nyingchi Mainling Airport")
The opening ceremony was held on the morning of September 9, 2015 for the [La-Lin Highway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La-Lin_Highway?action=edit&redlink=1 "La-Lin Highway \(page does not exist\)") [[zh](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E6%8B%89%E6%9E%97%E5%85%AC%E8%B7%AF "zh:拉林公路")] (Lhasa to Mozhugongka section) and (Gongbu Jiangda to Linzhi section) connecting [Lhasa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lhasa "Lhasa")-[Linzhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linzhi "Linzhi").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyingchi#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyingchi#cite_note-%E9%80%9A%E8%BD%A6-15) It takes about 5 hours to travel from [Lhasa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lhasa "Lhasa") to Nyingchi by a highway opened at the end of 2018.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyingchi#cite_note-16) Nyingchi is connected to Lhasa by the 435-kilometer [Lhasa–Nyingchi railway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lhasa%E2%80%93Nyingchi_railway "Lhasa–Nyingchi railway"), completed in 2021. The journey from Lhasa by train takes 2.5 hours.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyingchi#cite_note-17)
The [Linzhi Milin Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linzhi_Milin_Airport "Linzhi Milin Airport") was opened in Nyingchi in March 2017. Linzhi Airport initiated [RNP navigation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RNP_approach "RNP approach") procedures in 2006, becoming the first airport in China to operate exclusively with RNP.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyingchi#cite_note-18) It is presently the sole transportation airport globally where all aircraft takeoffs and landings are mandated to adhere to RNP AR procedures, necessitating compliance with specific aircraft and crew qualifications.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyingchi#cite_note-19) In 2018, the construction of the [Engineered materials arrestor system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Engineered_materials_arrestor_system "Engineered materials arrestor system") (EMAS) was completed at the Miling Airport.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyingchi#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyingchi#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyingchi#cite_note-22)

## Flora and fauna
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nyingchi&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Flora and fauna")]
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/da/Gongbo%27gyamda%2C_Nyingchi%2C_Tibet%2C_China_-_panoramio_%2819%29.jpg/250px-Gongbo%27gyamda%2C_Nyingchi%2C_Tibet%2C_China_-_panoramio_%2819%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Gongbo'gyamda,_Nyingchi,_Tibet,_China_-_panoramio_\(19\).jpg)[Basum Lake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basum_Tso "Basum Tso") in [Gongbo'gyamda County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gongbo'gyamda_County "Gongbo'gyamda County") [![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cd/Nyingchi_Landscape.jpg/250px-Nyingchi_Landscape.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Nyingchi_Landscape.jpg)View of the [Nyang River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyang_River "Nyang River") near Nyingchi
According to local forestry officials, Nyingchi hosts the country's largest primitive forest region that covers 26.4 billion cubic metres, storing over 800 million cubic metres of wood.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyingchi#cite_note-tibettravelplanner-28) The forests of Bome, Zayu and Lhoyu have ancient [dragon spruces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Picea_asperata "Picea asperata") which reach heights of over 80 metres and diameters of 2.5 metres. Wildlife species include "the Bengal tiger, leopard, bear, snub-nosed monkey, antelope and lesser panda."[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyingchi#cite_note-tibettravelplanner-28)
There are over 2,000 species of higher plants, including some 100 species of xylophyta, 165 species of medical herbs and fungus. Crops include rice, peanut, apple, orange, banana, and lemon. Agricultural products include medicinal materials, edible fungus, orange, tangerine, sugar cane, honey peach, apple, pear, grape, walnut and other fruits.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyingchi#cite_note-tibettravelplanner-28)
